sehemu: Part II: Members of Parliament, Constituencies and Election of Members
jina: Determination of question whether a person is a Member of Parliament
maudhui: (1) Every proceeding for the determination of the question - (a) whether the election or appointment of any person as a Member of Parliament was valid or not; or (b) whether a Member has ceased to be a Member and his seat in Parliament has become vacant or not, shall be instituted and heard in the first instance by the High Court of the United Republic of Tanzania, subject to subarticle (2). (2) Where the Electoral Commission, in exercising its powers under Article 41(7), declares any Member of Parliament to have been elected President, no court or other body shall further inquire into any matter concerning the vacancy of that Member's seat. (3) Parliament may enact a law making provision concerning: (a) persons who may institute proceedings in the High Court; (b) the grounds, times and procedure for instituting proceedings; and (c) the jurisdiction of the High Court over such proceedings and the procedure for hearing them. (4) There shall be a right of appeal to the Court of Appeal of Tanzania against a decision of the High Court in any proceeding heard under this Article.

(2) Where the Electoral Commission, in exercising its powers under Article 41(7), declares any Member of Parliament to have been elected President, no court or other body shall further inquire into any matter concerning the vacancy of that Member's seat.

(3) Parliament may enact a law making provision concerning: (a) persons who may institute proceedings in the High Court; (b) the grounds, times and procedure for instituting proceedings; and (c) the jurisdiction of the High Court over such proceedings and the procedure for hearing them.
(4) There shall be a right of appeal to the Court of Appeal of Tanzania against a decision of the High Court in any proceeding heard under this Article.
